full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha CJ : These appeals by leave are directed from a judgment of this court in Civil Petition Nos. 205 and 466 of 2006 dismissing the leave petitions summarily. Respondents in both the appeals are the plaintiffs who have instituted the suit for declaration of title in the suit land with a further declaration that the suit land is not an abandoned property and recovery of khas possession. 

 27. The court takes up the appeal for hearing. Mr Attorney-General has placed the impugned judgment along with the judgments of the other courts, and submits that from the above facts, there is no need to prove further that Hakim Syed Abdul Ali was not present in Bangladesh and his whereabouts is not known to the government; that he had ceased to occupy, supervise or manage the property after 25th March, 1971 and that the government legally took over the control and management of the property in 1972. He further contends that the relief (b) claimed in the suit for recovery of khas possession itself proves that the whereabouts of Hakim Syed Abdul Ali was not known to the government and accordingly, the government took control and management of the property. 28. Syed Sajjad Hossain Jayedi (PW 1) stated that before him, Abdus Salam and Mostafa were attorneys of the plaintiffs. This attorney is not alive and/or missing according to Moazzem's version. Even if it is assumed that the plaintiffs 1-3 are the heirs of Hakim Syed Abdul Ali, after the death of Syed Sajjad Hossain Jayedi, they did not authorise anybody else to conduct the suit, appeal, revision relating to the property which is apparent from the statements of Mohammad Shaheen and Moazzem .Hossain. In the suit the plaintiffs have examined four witnesses. Besides PW 1, Syed Jahangir All (PW 2) is a resident of Dhaka. He claimed that the plaintiff No. 4 Dr. Syed Abdul Wali, the brother of Hakim Syed Abdul Ali was not traceable in 1991. He claimed that when Hakim Syed Abdul Ali went to Kolkata for treatment he kept Syed Hyder Ali as caretaker of the property. He made completely a different story, inasmuch as, PW 1 stated that Hakim Syed Abdul All left the country in the first part of 1971 keeping the property under the care of MP Hyder Ali and that Dr. Syed A. Wali died in 1991 as bachelor. According to PW 1, Hakim Syed Abdul All died on 4-3-1971 and his death certificate was obtained on 25-10-1994, which is totally doubtful because he deposed on 23-8-1996. This proved that just immediately before deposing in the court, the death certificate was obtained. Where about of Dr. Syed A. Wali has not been properly explained. One says he died issueless and the other says he is not traceable.
